dossier.architecture: Differential drive with simple two-position launcher and tilting telescopic climb.

subsystems.intake: Collector has large printed mecanum ends; biased flaps and tread combat two-ball jams.
subsystems.transfer: Tall conveyor and rejection fork; infrared staging pauses a ball long enough for delayed color sensing.
subsystems.scoring: Two-position pneumatic elevation at fixed speed/distance; brass flywheel inertia and compliant passive Lexan/yoga-mat hood. Powered back roller was unfinished.
subsystems.endgame: Tilting telescope with passive hooks and rope-induced center-of-gravity movement; lighter plastic outer stage outperformed a heavier replacement that damaged bearings.
subsystems.controls: Color rejection disabled in autonomous to save time, enabled in teleop. Limited field practice informed simpler shot controls.

versions: Heavier aluminum climb stage was tried and rejected; do not describe it as the final improvement.
dossier.analysis: This is a valuable counterexample to copying the most complex elite architecture: development time and practice availability can make a discrete shot map and lower mechanical mass more effective.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.body:
# 2022-694: Sensor latency and passive hood compliance are deliberate constraints

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A tall conveyor and rejection fork pause cargo for delayed color sensing. Printed collector contacts and biased flaps address two-ball jams. The retained launcher uses added flywheel inertia and a compliant passive hood; an additional powered back roller was unfinished.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly prioritizes simpler scoring after pandemic-related experience gaps.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A deliberate staging pause can improve correct classification even when it lowers nominal feed speed. A passive hood saves actuation but must hold repeatable compression as material wears. Unfinished hardware cannot be credited as an explanation of observed shooting.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure classification latency, false rejection, two-ball recovery and trajectory drift as the hood material ages.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
